set_aside.subject: removed challenge and delivery models
set_aside.text: “The State 1 records M01–M37” contradicts State 1’s “The former models M08–M12 … are removed.”
set_aside.question: Does `models` own only the surviving numbered records, or must it still define M08–M12 because the inclusive M01–M37 range says so?
options: Treat M01–M37 as an inclusive range and retain M08–M12
Treat it as shorthand for the surviving indexed records and omit M08–M12
set_aside.default_guess: Omit M08–M12 and rewrite the range as an explicit surviving set.

witness.initial: The owner has removed email challenges and delivery, while State 3 still assigns `models` the records M01–M37.
events: A later agent generates the shared model module from State 3.
Another module or model-closure agent imports the resulting vocabulary.
outcomes: M08–M12 exist as unused challenge and delivery types because M01–M37 was read inclusively.
M08–M12 do not exist because State 1’s explicit removal was treated as controlling.
witness.observer: The model-closure, repository-port, and API code authors see different available types.

set_aside.subject: former challenge HTTP routes
set_aside.text: `api` owns “The staff, administrator and producer HTTP JSON routes of rules.http_router_backend,” while State 2 still carries “rules.http_router_backend (56 routes …)” from the pre-removal Factory spec, but R0-23 says “The portal has no email-challenge or password-reset operation.”
set_aside.question: Are the former verification, email-change, and password-reset routes removed from the router backend, or do the carried 56 routes remain present with their former inert behavior?
options: Remove the former challenge routes and define a new smaller route catalog
Keep the carried 56-route backend, including inert challenge routes
set_aside.default_guess: Remove the routes and update the router-backend route count and ownership text.

witness.initial: A deployment is assembled after R0-23 from the carried 56-route backend.
events: An unauthenticated caller sends a request to a former password-reset or email-confirmation path.
The HTTP router resolves or fails to resolve the path.
outcomes: The route is absent because the product has no such operation.
The route is present and returns its former concealed inert response because the carried router backend was retained.
witness.observer: The HTTP caller sees a routing response versus an operation response.

set_aside.subject: A10 ownership after removal
set_aside.text: “| A10 | `staff_identity` | — |” assigns no consumers even though the removal also changes `models` request/entity vocabulary, `api` routes, repository ports, persistence wiring, and runtime configuration.
set_aside.question: Which modules own the non-`staff_identity` consequences of A10, and how may those modules depend on the decision they must implement?
options: A10 has additional consumers such as `models`, `api`, `portal_store`, and `runtime_settings`
The removals are separate structural facts outside A10 and need their own explicitly owned record
`staff_identity` alone owns A10 and the other modules derive their removals without being consumers
set_aside.default_guess: Record the affected modules as consumers of the relevant parts of A10.

witness.initial: The old design contains challenge request types, repository ports, routes, settings, and delivery persistence; the new ownership map gives A10 only to `staff_identity`.
events: The owner removes the email feature.
Independent later agents generate the model vocabulary, router, and persistence closure using only their module responsibilities.
outcomes: Every agent infers the structural removals and produces a challenge-free system.
Only `staff_identity` and the three expressly removed modules change; orphan request types, ports, routes, or schema artifacts remain elsewhere.
witness.observer: Assembly authors and HTTP clients see different public surfaces and persistence schemas.
